rationale: Two empirically reproduced mode-fabrication paths survive on the reviewed commit (7b6d83f1), both in the beads-1/2 hard-block class the bead exists to close. (F1, deterministic) `state show --spec <unresolvable-or-invalid>` silently discards the explicit-target resolution error and answers from ambient discovery: with one draft on disk, `--spec 999` / `--spec 042` / `--spec 'not_a_valid_id!!'` all print {"mode":"spec","activeSpec":"129-foo",...} exit 0 — a confident answer about a spec the user did not ask about; with zero drafts, `--spec 999` prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0. Pre-bead code refused (non-zero "no active state found") on this path, so this is a regression introduced by the commit. (F2, one-flake race, reproduced with a stateful bd stub) a single transient bd failure followed by recovery fabricates idle: no-flag `state show` over an in_progress epic prints {"mode":"idle"} exit 0 (healthy-bd control on the identical fixture prints mode plan); the `--spec 131-active` variant prints {"mode":"idle","activeSpec":"131-active","specBranch":"spec/131-active"} exit 0 — the literal idle-alongside-non-empty-activeSpec shape AC-1(i) bans, and a direct violation of R1.4's "never fabricate a mode from a failed read" plus the new ADR-0023 amendment's own closing sentence. Root causes are small and local (see concrete changes). Everything else held up under attack: unreadable SpecsDir / ENOTDIR / branch-check git failures / spec-dir permission errors all refuse with the ADR-0035 recovery line (verified empirically); symlinked and half-created drafts skip silently but match spec.List's house convention and OQ-2's both-exist definition; the concurrent-approve race is benign single-snapshot staleness; deviation A is sound within this verb (assessment in findings). The three AC-1 tests, internal/resolve, and internal/lint pass; the five cmd/mindspec next-ready-gate failures I hit reproduce identically at parent commit f12ce273, so they are pre-existing on this host, not bead-3 regressions.
concrete_changes_required: F1 — cmd/mindspec/state.go resolveErr branch (state.go:80-133): when specFlag != "", propagate resolveErr instead of falling into ambient draft discovery/idle. The draft carve-out and the bare-idle conclusion are only legitimate when NO explicit target was given (or, if you want prefix-targets-draft to work, scope the probe to the requested spec via draftSpecStatusWithCache — but the minimum honest fix is propagation). Repro: fixture repo with draft 129-foo only; `mindspec state show --spec 999` → {"mode":"spec","activeSpec":"129-foo"} exit 0; with no drafts → {"mode":"idle"} exit 0; `--spec 'not_a_valid_id!!'` → same fabrication. Add regression tests for: unresolvable prefix with 1 draft, with 0 drafts, and an invalid --spec value — all must refuse non-zero naming the resolution failure.

F2a — internal/resolve/resolve.go ResolveModeWithCache (resolve.go:~66-75): a genuine (non-not-found) error from FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache currently routes into the draft probe; when the probe's AllEpics health-retry succeeds (errors are not memoized in phase.Cache) and the now-warm epic lookup finds the epic, isDraft=false collapses to ModeIdle — discarding both the original error AND the epic just found. Either distinguish the not-found sentinel from genuine failures before entering the draft probe, or have draftSpecStatusWithCache surface the epicID it found so the caller derives the real phase instead of assuming idle. Repro (stateful bd stub failing exactly call 1, in_progress epic for 131-active, spec dir+branch present): `mindspec state show --spec 131-active` → {"mode":"idle","activeSpec":"131-active","specBranch":"spec/131-active"} exit 0 — AC-1(i)'s banned shape.

F2b — cmd/mindspec/state.go (state.go:92-103): after the c.AllEpics() health probe succeeds, the code concludes "bd healthy, nothing active" without re-running target resolution — but if ResolveTargetWithCache's failure WAS the bd flake, the now-warm cache contains active epics the code never re-consults. Re-run resolution (free — memoized) after a successful probe, or gate the probe-then-proceed path on the resolveErr being the benign no-active-specs case. Repro: same stub, no flag → {"mode":"idle"} exit 0; healthy-bd control on the identical fixture → {"mode":"plan","activeSpec":"131-active"}.

F3 (minor, may fold into F1) — multi-draft + explicit --spec prefix: with drafts 129-foo and 130-bar, `state show --spec 129` refuses with "multiple active specs found; use --spec to target one" — honest refusal, contradictory advice (the flag WAS passed and uniquely prefixes one draft; the full ID works). Propagating resolveErr per F1 restores the correct "no spec found matching prefix" text; prefix resolution over drafts can be a follow-up.

findings.title: Explicit --spec resolution failure silently swallowed; state show answers about a different spec (or idle) with exit 0
findings.detail: state.go's resolveErr branch never consults specFlag. ResolveSpecPrefixWithCache errors (unmatched numeric prefix, invalid ID) are discarded except for the ErrAmbiguousTarget type-assert, and the command proceeds to ambient draft discovery. Empirical: one-draft fixture, healthy stub bd → `--spec 999`, `--spec 042`, and `--spec 'not_a_valid_id!!'` each print the DRAFT's {"mode":"spec","activeSpec":"129-foo"} exit 0; zero-draft fixture → {"mode":"idle"} exit 0. The pre-bead code refused non-zero here ("no active state found"), so the exit-0 fabrication is introduced by this commit. None of the 10 new tests exercise --spec in the fallback branch.

findings.title: Single transient bd failure + recovery fabricates idle — including AC-1(i)'s literally banned idle-with-activeSpec shape
findings.detail: phase.Cache does not memoize errors, so the AllEpics health probes retry. Path a (resolve.go): FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache fails (bd call 1) → draft probe entered → health retry (call 2) succeeds → epic found warm → isDraft=false → ModeIdle returned, original error and found epic both discarded. Path b (state.go): ResolveTargetWithCache fails on the flake → health retry succeeds → code assumes nothing active without re-resolving against the warm cache → draft scan → idle. Empirical (bd stub failing exactly its first call; in_progress epic 131-active; spec dir + spec/131-active branch present, as for any mid-lifecycle spec): no-flag → {"mode":"idle"} exit 0 (control: {"mode":"plan"}); --spec 131-active → {"mode":"idle","activeSpec":"131-active","specBranch":"spec/131-active"} exit 0. Violates R1.4 verbatim and the ADR-0023 amendment's own sentence: "a failure of either propagates rather than being fabricated into a mode".

findings.title: Multi-draft + --spec prefix returns self-contradictory advice
findings.detail: Two drafts + `--spec 129` → non-zero ErrAmbiguousTarget "use --spec to target one" although --spec was passed and uniquely prefixes 129-foo (full ID works). The correct "no spec found matching prefix" error is also replaced by the ambiguity listing for arbitrary unmatched prefixes (`--spec 999`). Folds into the F1 fix.

findings.title: Judgment call A: acceptable within this verb; the real divergence risk is F2's error-path fork, not the plan's feared split
findings.detail: Within state show, phase.ResolveContext is fully removed and one Cache sources mode, activeBead, and specBranch from the same resolved specID — R1.2's letter ("one derivation authoritative, the other removed") is satisfied for this verb, and the implementer's regression argument is verified: ResolveContextFromDirWithCache's WorktreeMain path derives ambiguity from CWD ignoring --spec, so the literal substitution would break `state show --spec <one-of-several>`. Instruct tails still on ResolveContext are bead 5's stated territory — a disagreement window bead 5 must close, not a contradiction now. However, P7 (F2) shows the retained 'single' derivation self-diverges on its internal error-path fork — fixing F2 is what actually makes the one-derivation claim trustworthy.

findings.title: Hardened paths verified; skip conventions consistent; pre-existing test failures identified
findings.detail: Verified refusals (non-zero, ADR-0035 recovery line): unreadable SpecsDir (chmod 000), SpecsDir ReadDir non-ENOENT errors, branch-check git failures (BranchExistsIn returns error for non-exit-1), spec-dir stat permission errors. Symlinked spec dirs (DirEntry.IsDir()=false) and half-created drafts (dir w/o branch, branch w/o dir) are silently invisible → idle; this matches spec.List's identical skip convention and OQ-2's both-must-exist definition — acceptable, worth a one-line doc note at most. Concurrent spec-approve race: single memoized AllEpics snapshot → at worst stale by one invocation, honest TOCTOU. Composition-allowlist entries house-pattern conformant; ADR-0023 amendment appropriately narrow (no general spec-artifact-authority leak). Tests: the three AC-1 legs + internal/resolve + internal/lint PASS in the bead worktree; five cmd/mindspec TestNextReadyGate*/TestBeadReadyCheck* failures (stale .mindspec/phase.lock in fixtures) reproduce identically at parent commit f12ce273 → pre-existing on this host, NOT bead-3 regressions. Worktree left byte-identical at 7b6d83f1.
